problems.description: 75 convention violations concentrated in devserver.ts and markdown.ts: functions/classes/interfaces and constants use non-conventional naming (appears to be Python snake_case leaking into TypeScript) rather than camelCase/PascalCase/UPPER_CASE, dragging convention score to 0.51

Deleted the seed index.ts (93 lines) wholesale instead of evolving or inheriting its patterns — the baseline Express/Todo structure was discarded in favor of a brand-new SSG layout, so no existing architectural seams were preserved
+4571/-93 lines in a single session commit is a large unbroken change surface for session 1, making it harder to isolate which introduced patterns will need correction later

strengths: SonarQube deltas are strongly positive: 0 new bugs, -14 smells, -40 cognitive complexity, -7.9% duplications
Clean modular scaffolding: separated src modules (devserver, markdown), jest/ts-jest config, package.json bin entry to dist/cli.js
Tests included via src/__tests__ layout and configured testMatch
commit_reviews.summary: Solid modular architecture with strong SonarQube gains, but net-negative on conventions (75 naming violations, 0.51 score) and it discarded the seed's existing patterns entirely, so despite the quality metrics the commit lands worse than baseline.

problems.description: Adding handlebars (4.7.9) pulls a sizeable transitive dependency tree (uglify-js, minimist, neo-async, source-map) into production for what appears to be lightweight templating; a smaller alternative might fit an SSG better. The lockfile changes correctly promote these to prod deps, so the bookkeeping itself is right.

Measured convention score is 0.51 with 75 violations, but the flagged violations (devserver.ts, markdown.ts camelCase/PascalCase/UPPER_CASE) are in pre-existing files not touched by this commit. The new templates.ts and test files use proper camelCase/PascalCase, so the low score reflects accumulated codebase style debt, not this commit.

strengths: Thorough test coverage for the new TemplateEngine: built-in defaults, on-disk templates/partials/layouts, XSS title escaping, raw-HTML passthrough, and graceful fallback to default template/layout when frontmatter names are missing
Small, focused feature diff (+401/-67, +1 function) with +0 bugs, +0.0% duplication, and cognitive complexity reduced by 10
Respects existing patterns: test file placed in the established __tests__ directory and dependency additions made consistently in both package.json and package-lock.json
commit_reviews.summary: A clean, well-tested feature commit that fits the SSG architecture and follows existing patterns; the low measured convention score (0.51) is attributable to pre-existing style violations in untouched files (devserver.ts, markdown.ts), not to code introduced here.

problems.description: 75 naming-case violations across devserver.ts and markdown.ts (functions not camelCase, classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE), matching the mechanical convention score of 0.51

Adds chokidar + ws along with their transitive graph (anymatch, readdirp, binary-extensions, glob-parent, fsevents), promoting several packages from dev to runtime in package-lock.json — acceptable for the feature but a broader dependency surface
Dev server integration (file watching + WebSocket live reload) appears concentrated in new devserver.ts rather than decomposed into smaller modules; only +5 functions for a net +463 lines

strengths: Uses well-established ecosystem libraries (chokidar, ws) instead of hand-rolled file watching or sockets
SonarQube deltas are strongly positive: smells -14, cognitive complexity -11, duplications -7.7%, bugs +0
Commits package-lock.json, keeping the dependency graph reproducible
Feature is architecturally coherent — a live-reload dev server is a natural integration step for a static site generator
commit_reviews.summary: Session 3 adds a coherent dev-server integration (chokidar + ws) with real quality improvements but is dragged down by 75 naming-convention violations in the new/edited TS files, matching the low 0.51 convention score.

problems.description: BuildContext uses an `[key: string]: any` index signature (src/plugin.ts), which erases type safety for plugin context fields and lets typos/undefined fields pass silently at compile time.
Dynamic config/plugin loading relies on CommonJS `require()` (src/cli.ts, src/ssg.ts) in a TS module project; this is inconsistent with ESM imports and bypasses bundler/type checking.
Silent try/catch with empty bodies in loadCliConfig, loadPlugins, and loadFromConfig swallows config errors and falls back to defaults, making misconfiguration undetectable.
DevServerPlugin opens a server in onStart but never closes it (no onEnd implementation), leaking the port/listener for long-lived embedders.
Plugin ordering is implicit and undocumented — TemplatePlugin's onFile/afterBuild assume MarkdownPlugin populated context.pages first; no dependency declaration or validation.
loadCliConfig rebuilds the options object and drops the `config` key and any plugin entries, so a CLI-provided config path is lost after the merge.

strengths: Clean separation of concerns — markdown parsing, templating, and dev serving are decomposed into focused plugins with a clear lifecycle (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd).
Consistent use of TypeScript interfaces (Plugin, BuildContext, SsgConfig) with a coherent public API re-exported via src/index.ts.
Mechanical metrics support the refactor: cognitive complexity -46, smells -4, duplications -2.1%, 0 new bugs.
Graceful nullability handling (context.engine!) and defensive fallbacks in the SSG constructor provide sensible defaults.
commit_reviews.summary: Net-positive refactor that reduces complexity (-46 cognitive, -4 smells) and introduces a well-structured plugin lifecycle, though it trades some type safety for extensibility via the `any` index signature and swallows config errors — with the note that the 0.51 convention score and its listed violations (e.g., flagging already-camelCase functions) appear to be analyzer false positives, as the code itself follows camelCase functions and PascalCase types.

problems.description: 75 naming-convention violations reported across devserver.ts and markdown.ts (functions should be camelCase, classes/interfaces PascalCase, constants UPPER_CASE); convention score 0.51. Note: these files are outside the visible test diff — the +3-file change implies the agent edited production cross-cutting code, not just tests.

Duplications +1.8% and cognitive complexity +179 in the added test file: full Page objects are inlined ~15 times instead of using the defined makePage helper, and repeated writeMarkdownFile calls re-duplicate fixture setup.
+6 new SonarQube smells introduced; complex inlined fixtures obscure test intent and make future fixture changes multi-site edits.

strengths: Comprehensive behavioral coverage of incremental builds: clean build, skip-unchanged, rebuild-changed, clean flag, added pages, deleted-page cache pruning.
Tests use tmp dirs with beforeEach/afterEach cleanup and only touch the public surface (generateSiteIncremental, CacheManager), so no production code is modified in the visible diff.
Helper functions makePage and writeMarkdownFile establish a reusable, type-checked fixture pattern despite being underused.
commit_reviews.summary: Well-scoped incremental-build test suite with real behavioral value, but dragged down by fixture duplication and 75 naming-convention violations in the production files also touched by the commit.

compounding_issues: Session 1 committed node_modules (5197 files) and dist/ build artifacts into version control, flooding every later diff with dependency churn; only dist/ was ever cleaned up (session 5), node_modules remains committed

Session 4's plugin refactor created a parallel architecture (SSG class + plugin lifecycle) that coexists with the original generator.ts/CLI path instead of replacing it; cli.ts, server.ts, and incremental.ts all still drive the old pipeline, so the system now has two overlapping build paths
The SSG serve() path is incomplete: it runs plugin onStart/onEnd but never builds, serves, or wires rebuilds, leaving the DevServerPlugin server orphaned from the plugin pipeline
Template rendering logic (renderPage + renderLayout + index) is duplicated three times across generator.ts, plugins/template.ts, and incremental.ts
key_decisions: Session 1 rebuilt from scratch: replaced the seed Express Todo API with a TypeScript + Jest static-site-generator CLI (parser, generator, types) rather than evolving the seed
Session 2 adopted Handlebars with a layout/partials template hierarchy driven by page frontmatter
Session 3 added a dev server with live rebuild via http + WebSocket + chokidar watching
Session 4 introduced a plugin lifecycle architecture (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) plus SsgConfig and ssg.config.ts for extension points
Session 5 added an incremental build cache keyed on source-file and template hashes with a persistent manifest, and removed dist/ from version control
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose steadily across the story. Session 1 delivered a clean, well-tested minimal core (parser/generator/CLI). Session 2 extended it naturally with a Handlebars template system and tests. Session 3 integrated a live-reload dev server. Session 4 was the most ambitious but the roughest — it introduced a plugin architecture that was only half-wired into the existing build path, leaving a duplicated, incompletely integrated serve() route. Session 5 recovered momentum with a solid, hash-based incremental build (dedicated cache module, manifest, focused tests) and finally removed built artifacts from the repo. Test coverage grew at every session, so despite the session-4 architectural wobble the codebase became broader and more polished overall.
story_review.summary: A largely coherent greenfield-to-feature-complete progression that improved each session, with the main blemish being a session-4 plugin refactor that created a half-integrated parallel build path and the persistent problem of committed node_modules.
